security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel in HS-mode writes to mpmpdeleg.pmpnum to increase the PMP share, which implicitly reduces hspmpdeleg.pmpnum below the index of a locked hSPMP entry, causing a hypervisor-locked protection entry to silently fall into the vSPMP region where it can be unlocked via vsireg2.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: write to mpmpdeleg CSR without first ensuring no locked hSPMP entries exist at indices >= (total_pmp_entries - new_mpmpdeleg_value - current_hspmpdeleg_value_saturated)
security_spec.summary: mpmpdeleg writes can implicitly shrink hspmpdeleg below locked hSPMP entry indices, silently converting locked hypervisor protections into vSPMP entries bypassable via vsireg2 unlock

findings.finding: The Linux kernel contains no SPMP (S-mode PMP) support, no PMP delegation CSR definitions (mpmpdeleg, hspmpdeleg, spmpdeleg, pmpdeleg), no sireg2/vsireg2 CSR definitions, and no KVM SPMP virtualization code. The only PMP support present is standard M-mode PMP (CSR_PMPCFG0/CSR_PMPADDR0) with bit constants PMP_R/W/X/A/L. The spec's vulnerability condition — writing to mpmpdeleg without checking locked hSPMP entry indices — cannot manifest because the kernel has zero code paths that touch mpmpdeleg or any SPMP-related CSR.
findings.snippet:
#define CSR_PMPCFG0  0x3a0
#define CSR_PMPADDR0 0x3b0
/* PMP configuration */
#define PMP_R        0x01
#define PMP_W        0x02
#define PMP_X        0x04
#define PMP_A        0x18
#define PMP_A_TOR    0x08
#define PMP_A_NA4    0x10
#define PMP_A_NAPOT  0x18
#define PMP_L        0x80
/* No SPMP, mpmpdeleg, hspmpdeleg, or spmpdeleg definitions exist */
